subject: Glacier Energy — Dedicated capacity runbook and renewal
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@glacierenergy.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@glacierenergy.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Glacier Q4 launch — anticipated capacity bump and renewal window

Hi Stephanie,

Quick heads-up: our product team just locked the Q4 launch date and we expect a material uptick in large-context assistant traffic. Renewal for our Dedicated cluster is coming up in July and procurement asked me to come to you with expected QPS/token growth and an initial sizing ask so we can speed the amendment.

High-level: new feature will increase multi-turn assistant usage (average ~1.2k tokens/request today, projected to ~1.8k at peak) and a marketing campaign will create a 6–8 week ramp. We're looking for options to:
- increase committed GPU capacity for predictable throughput
- enable a burst/reserved pool for launches
- get throughput guarantees for p95/p99 latencies during business hours

I've attached our internal forecast (glacier-q4-q1-qps-forecast.csv). Can your team propose a runbook and a recommended GPU commitment for renewal? Procurement wants rough numbers by end of next week.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min sync if that helps.

—Lena
Director, Product 
Glacier Energy
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@glacierenergy.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Glacier Q4 launch — anticipated capacity bump and renewal window

Lena — thanks for the note and the forecast. This is exactly the kind of heads-up we want ahead of renewals.

Quick asks so we size conservatively:
- Can you confirm peak concurrency windows (timezone + hours) and whether the marketing campaign will be front-loaded (first 2 weeks) or sustained?
- Are there hard SLA targets you need for p95/p99 (token latency) or is p99 < 900ms sufficient?
- Do you plan to keep the same model family in production or test a quantized variant during the ramp?

I'll put together a preliminary runbook with two scenarios: Baseline commit (12-month), and Launch Burst (12-week reserved burst pool). Will include GPU counts (H100 vs A100 80GB tradeoffs), a throughput SLO proposal, and a cost delta.

If you can drop the CSV in a shared drive or confirm the spikes per timezone, I can turn this around in 48 hours. If useful, I can schedule a 30-min sync with Karthik (SE) and Marissa (AM) for deep-dive.

–Steph
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Diego Sosa <diego.sosa@glacierenergy.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@glacierenergy.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Glacier Q4 launch — anticipated capacity bump and renewal window

Thanks Steph — attaching the cleaned forecast (same CSV) and a short note on traffic shape.

TL;DR:
- Baseline today: 120 QPS average (US/EU business hrs), peak bursts to ~280 QPS during product tests.
- New feature projection: baseline to 220 QPS within 6 weeks of launch, peak bursts up to 520 QPS.
- Token profile: median 1,200 tokens/request; 95th percentile ~1,800 tokens; we have many multi-turn sessions that keep KV cache warm.
- Priority: keep p99 < 800ms during business hours; cost is secondary but we need predictability for budgeting.

We'll accept a proposal for mixing committed H100s for low-latency endpoints and A100s for background batch/embedding. Procurement prefers a single amendment (commit + term) rather than multiple PO changes.

Diego
Platform Ops
Glacier Energy

Attachment: glacier-q4-q1-qps-forecast.csv
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@glacierenergy.com>, Diego Sosa <diego.sosa@glacierenergy.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed runbook + sizing (baseline & burst) for Glacier renewal

Hi team — apologies for the long note, wanted to capture a clear set of options so procurement has actionable choices. Summary + recommended next steps below. Full analysis attached (proposed-gpu-mix.pdf).

Executive summary:
- Recommended baseline commit (12 months): 16 H100 (80GB) instances in reserved pool. This supports an expected steady-state of ~240 QPS at ~1.2k tokens/request with p95 < 350ms and p99 < 700ms for 2k token prompts using our optimized kernels and KV cache.
- Launch Burst (12-week add-on, optional): 6 additional H100s to be kept as a burst reserve (can be warm-started on 30 min notice). This covers forecasted peaks to ~520 QPS and keeps p99 under 900ms during sustained bursts.
- Cost trade: a baseline of 16 H100s vs 24 A100 80GBs — H100s deliver ~25–40% lower p99 on long-context prompts; A100s are ~18% cheaper/month but may require more instances and yield higher p99 during peak. We include both pricing lines in attachment.

Throughput guarantees and fallbacks:
- Proposal: throughput SLO of 400 QPS sustained during business hours (US/EU overlap), with p99 < 900ms. If we detect sustained >10% headroom breach for 3 consecutive hours, automatic fallback to model-quantized variants + burst pool will be triggered (reduces cost but increases p99 by ~150–250ms).

Operational runbook highlights:
- Ramp plan: 0–2 weeks monitoring, 2–6 weeks progressive traffic shift, 6–12 weeks steady-state with burst enabled.
- Observability: 30-day request-level traces, token-level cost breakdown, and daily runway report to Glacier.
- Change control: any permanent upsize requires 14-day notice and a short maintenance window for kernel tuning.

Action items for procurement if you choose baseline+burst:
1) Approve baseline commit: 16 H100s, 12-month term.
2) Approve burst add-on: 6 H100s for 12 weeks (non-committed, billed on usage but reserved capacity at burst priority).
3) Sign amendment (we'll generate a DocuSign link) for revised commit and SLAs.

Questions:
- Does the team want the cheaper A100 line in the amendment as an alternate?
- Are you OK with the proposed SLO and automatic fallback to quantized models?

If you want, we can also provide a 6-month ramp term (reduce baseline to 12 H100s for first 6 months while enabling a larger burst pool).

Thanks — I can convert this to a one-page term sheet for procurement.

–Steph
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-gpu-mix.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed runbook + sizing (baseline & burst) for Glacier renewal

Steph / Marissa — quick technical notes on the H100 vs A100 tradeoffs and an alternative hybrid mapping we should surface to Glacier:

- H100s: best-in-class for long-context (2k+ tokens) p99 and lower memory-bandwidth overhead for KV cache. Recommended for the conversational endpoints where p99 matters.
- A100 80GB: cost-effective for batch/embedding workloads and lower concurrency per-card for long contexts. If Glacier can route embeddings or batched rerank outside the low-latency endpoints, we can shave cost by running that on A100s.

Hybrid proposal (to include in options):
- Baseline reserved pool: 12 H100 (chat-critical) + 8 A100 (background embedding & rerank). This hybrid supports the forecasted steady-state with slightly higher p99 (~150ms delta) but reduces committed spend ~12% vs all-H100 baseline.
- Burst pool: 6 H100s for low-latency spikes.

Model/runtime suggestions:
- Default production: redwood-chat-2k-int8 (latency-optimized quantized variant).
- Fallback on sustained breach: redwood-chat-2k-q4f16 (lower precision, higher throughput).

I'll prepare an internal cost/latency matrix with expected token throughput per-card and cc you both. If procurement pushes hard on price, hybrid is a good negotiation lever.

—Karthik
Principal SE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Lena Park <lena.park@glacierenergy.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Sosa <diego.sosa@glacierenergy.com>, procurement <procurement@glacierenergy.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed runbook + sizing (baseline & burst) for Glacier renewal

Steph / team — thanks for the thorough plan and the hybrid option. Procurement reviewed the numbers and we want to proceed with the hybrid baseline you suggested: 12 H100 + 8 A100, plus the 6 H100 burst pool for the first 12 weeks. We agree to a 12-month term with a 20% discount on list for the committed baseline.

Next steps from our side: procurement will expect the amendment and a DocuSign link; we also want the observability add-on (90-day retention) and daily runway reports during the ramp. Please loop in legal and send the amendment by EOD Thursday so we can hit our July renewal cutoff.

I'll expect the DocuSign link and the AM to coordinate the implementation window.

—Lena
Director, Product
Glacier Energy
